body.statement: For every fixed \(r\) and every \(c\in[\underline c,\overline c]\), there exist dimensions \(N,T\to\infty\) and deterministic arrays \(d,qvec,a,b,\Lambda,F\) such that \(c_N\to c\), \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}})\), \(\Lambda^{\top}d=\Lambda^{\top}a_S=0\), \(F^{\top}qvec=F^{\top}b_S=0\), the full Gram limits \(N^{-1}\Lambda^{\top}\Lambda\) and \(T^{-1}F^{\top}F\) are positive definite, the selector-restricted limits \(N^{-1}\Lambda^{\top}M_d\Lambda\) and \(T^{-1}F^{\top}M_{qvec}F\) are positive definite, and the loading, factor, and treatment-score rows are uniformly bounded. Hence the exact-oracle triangular-array class is nonempty without imposing any rule for selecting a minimizer of \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\).
body.justification: The sensitivity experiment must contain concrete deterministic sequences rather than rely on mutually inconsistent oracle restrictions.
body.gap: This is a nonvacuity certificate for the paper's abstract class, not a claim that the restrictions are observable or operationally constructible.
body.consumer: It validates that the absorption phase law is evaluated on a nonempty confounding-free oracle class.
